eligibilityNote: Compared all available economics laureate names in the official Nobel API with these nine names; no match. Primary institutional profiles reviewed for identity and living-status indicators. Recheck immediately before opening.

candidates.name: Timothy Bresnahan
candidates.summary: Made market power and competition measurable, developing empirical methods for studying how firms behave in concentrated industries.
honors: BBVA Frontiers of Knowledge Award · announced 2018

papers.title: The oligopoly solution concept is identified
Empirical studies of industries with market power

candidates.reason: A mature empirical-IO prize case, with an explicit Cowen prediction alongside Pakes. Adds the identification and market-power side of this research cluster.

candidates.name: Samuel Kortum
candidates.summary: Built quantitative trade models connecting technology, geography and specialization, and used them to understand international trade patterns.
candidates.reason: A foundational quantitative-trade case. Decker's 2025 essay explicitly includes Kortum in a forward prediction for a 2026 trade prize; this is one commentator's view, not a consensus.

candidates.name: Whitney Newey
candidates.summary: Developed tools for robust inference and semiparametric estimation, including the widely used Newey–West covariance estimator.

papers.title: A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix
Large sample estimation and hypothesis testing

candidates.reason: A mature, distinctive econometrics contribution, reinforced by the 2026 Nemmers Prize. The award supports inclusion; it is not an annual Nobel forecast.

candidates.name: Drew Fudenberg
candidates.summary: Advanced the theory of repeated games, reputation and learning, explaining how strategic behavior evolves over time.
honors: Member of the National Academy of Sciences

papers.title: The Folk Theorem in Repeated Games with Discounting or with Incomplete Information

candidates.reason: A mature dynamic-game and learning case. Fudenberg is on Tol's principal ten-name 2026 list; that is one model-based forecast, not a consensus ranking.

candidates.name: Matthew Jackson
candidates.summary: Explained how social and economic networks form, and how their structure shapes incentives, information and economic outcomes.
honors: Member of the National Academy of Sciences

papers.title: A Strategic Model of Social and Economic Networks

candidates.reason: A distinctive networks and economic-theory case. Tol mentions Jackson as a possible co-recipient, not as a member of the principal ten-name forecast.

candidates.name: Andreu Mas-Colell
candidates.summary: Developed mathematical foundations for general equilibrium and contributed to adaptive learning and correlated equilibrium in games.

sources.label: BSE faculty, honors and research profile

papers.title: The Theory of General Economic Equilibrium: A Differentiable Approach
A Simple Adaptive Procedure Leading to Correlated Equilibrium

candidates.reason: A substantial general-equilibrium and theory case, supported by primary research and major-award evidence. Current market listing is additional attention, not expert endorsement.

candidates.name: Victor Chernozhukov
candidates.summary: Developed econometric inference methods that combine high-dimensional controls and machine learning with credible causal estimation.

sources.label: MIT IDSS research and honors profile

papers.title: Double/debiased machine learning for treatment and structural parameters
Inference on Treatment Effects after Selection among High-Dimensional Controls

candidates.reason: A distinctive modern-econometrics contribution warrants a place in the mature pool. The additional signals are a public market listing and a broad future longlist, not an independently verified 2026 expert forecast.

candidates.name: Luigi Zingales
candidates.summary: Studied corporate governance, financing and the value of control, connecting financial institutions with competition and political influence.

sources.label: Chicago Booth faculty and honors profile

papers.title: What Do We Know about Capital Structure? Some Evidence from International Data
What Determines the Value of Corporate Votes?

candidates.reason: A substantive corporate-finance and governance record supports the broader watchlist. Current prediction-market listing is weak attention evidence and does not on its own justify featured-favorite status.

candidates.name: John Haltiwanger
candidates.summary: Showed how job creation, job destruction and productivity growth emerge from firm entry, exit and reallocation, and helped build the longitudinal data used to study business dynamism.

papers.title: Who Creates Jobs? Small versus Large versus Young
Reallocation, Firm Turnover, and Efficiency: Selection on Productivity or Profitability?

candidates.reason: A mature empirical case in firm dynamics, job flows and productivity, with major research recognition. Cowen and Tabarrok discussed his data-building contribution as deserving Nobel recognition in 2024; that is historical advocacy, not a verified 2026 forecast.
